records.title: InputDevice sources and per-device services
records.summary: How an app learns what an input device is and what it offers, including the only standard hook for vibrators on input devices.
details: SOURCE_STYLUS (API 14): the device is a stylus pointing source.
SOURCE_BLUETOOTH_STYLUS (API 23): a Bluetooth stylus.
getMotionRange(axis): the real range and resolution of each axis, such as AXIS_PRESSURE.
getBatteryState() (API 31): battery of the input device, if it reports one.
getLightsManager() (API 31): lights on the input device.
getVibratorManager() (API 31): vibrators that belong to the input device. getVibrator() is deprecated since API 31.
No source has been found showing a stylus motor exposed through getVibratorManager().
records.basis: InputDevice reference, read on 2 Nov 2026.

records.title: Low-latency inking libraries
records.summary: Jetpack libraries that cut perceived pen latency. Haptics should line up with these strokes, so they matter for timing.
details: androidx.graphics:graphics-core: GLFrontBufferedRenderer draws the live stroke straight to the front buffer, then commit() redraws normally on ACTION_UP. Android 10 (API 29) and later.
View.requestUnbufferedDispatch(event): deliver motion events as soon as they arrive instead of batched per frame.
androidx.input:input-motionprediction: MotionEventPredictor.record() and predict() fill the gap with predicted points. Replace them with real data when it arrives.
Ink API (androidx.ink): brushes, stroke rendering, geometry and storage.
ML Kit Digital Ink Recognition: handwriting to text and gesture recognition.
Latency sources named by Google: pen registration with the touchscreen, touch sampling rate (60 to 1000 Hz), app processing, rendering.
records.basis: Advanced stylus features guide, read on 2 Nov 2026.

records.title: MotionEvent stylus data
records.summary: What an app receives from a stylus on any Android device: position, pressure, tilt, orientation, hover distance, tool type and cancellation flags.
details: Tool type per pointer: getToolType(i) returns TOOL_TYPE_STYLUS or TOOL_TYPE_ERASER.
AXIS_PRESSURE: normally 0 to 1, but can exceed 1 depending on calibration. Clamp or normalise.
AXIS_TILT: radians, 0 is perpendicular to the screen, pi/2 is flat.
AXIS_ORIENTATION: radians, 0 to pi clockwise or 0 to -pi counter-clockwise.
AXIS_DISTANCE (API 14): hover distance, 0 is contact. Values vary by maker; don't rely on exact numbers.
Hover actions: ACTION_HOVER_MOVE (API 12), ACTION_HOVER_ENTER and ACTION_HOVER_EXIT (API 14).
Palm rejection: ACTION_CANCEL, and FLAG_CANCELED (API 33) on a pointer-up that was an accidental touch. Undo that pointer's stroke.
Android 14 and later also send stylus button presses as KeyEvents (from the AOSP stylus spec).
Nothing in MotionEvent controls feedback. It is input only.
records.basis: Android developer guide and MotionEvent reference, read on 2 Nov 2026.

records.title: Android Bluetooth stylus HID descriptor
records.summary: The HID report a Bluetooth stylus sends so Android can merge it with touchscreen input.
details: Digitizer usage page, Pen and Stylus usages.
Tip Pressure, 10-bit (0 to 1023) in the example.
1-bit Barrel Switch, Secondary Barrel Switch, Tip Switch and Invert (eraser end).
Transducer Serial Number as a 128-bit feature report.
The descriptor may declare any subset of these, as long as it matches what the pen reports.
May also carry battery level and charging status.
Defines no output report for haptics.
records.basis: AOSP stylus page, read on 2 Nov 2026.

records.title: Vibrator, VibratorManager and VibrationEffect
records.summary: Android's haptics API. It drives the tablet's or phone's own actuator, not a stylus.
details: createOneShot(ms, amplitude) and createWaveform(timings, amplitudes, repeat): API 26. Amplitude 1 to 255 or DEFAULT_AMPLITUDE (-1).
createPredefined(id), API 29: EFFECT_CLICK 0, EFFECT_DOUBLE_CLICK 1, EFFECT_TICK 2, EFFECT_HEAVY_CLICK 5.

startComposition(), API 30, with primitives: CLICK 1, THUD 2 (API 31), SPIN 3 (API 31), QUICK_RISE 4, SLOW_RISE 5, QUICK_FALL 6, TICK 7, LOW_TICK 8 (API 31). Check support with Vibrator.arePrimitivesSupported().
Duration targets used by Android for estimates: CLICK 12 ms, TICK 5 ms, LOW_TICK 12 ms, QUICK_FALL 100 ms, QUICK_RISE 150 ms, SPIN 150 ms, THUD 300 ms, SLOW_RISE 500 ms.

API 36 adds composition delay types (DELAY_TYPE_PAUSE, DELAY_TYPE_RELATIVE_START_OFFSET), createRepeatingEffect(), and envelope builders (BasicEnvelopeBuilder, WaveformEnvelopeBuilder) for more consistent feel across devices.
VibratorManager (API 31) lists the device's vibrators. InputDevice.getVibratorManager() returns one for an input device.
records.basis: VibrationEffect and Composition reference, read on 2 Nov 2026.

records.title: UICanvasFeedbackGenerator (iPadOS)
records.summary: Apple's event-based canvas haptics: the app reports what happened, the system decides how it feels.
details: Available from iOS and iPadOS 17.5.
alignmentOccurred(at:): an object snapped to a guide.
pathCompleted(at:): a path finished or a shape was recognised.
Plays on Apple Pencil Pro with a compatible iPad. Playback is not guaranteed; the system weighs device, app state and battery.
There is no continuous texture API. That is the opposite of the OnePlus and Windows inking model.
records.basis: Apple documentation via search results, 2 Nov 2026.

records.title: cps8601_firmware.bin (pen charger firmware)
records.summary: 15 KB firmware for the tablet-side pen charging chip. It covers power transfer and the pen's in-band packets, with nothing about haptics.
details: Path: /odm/firmware/wireless_pen/<prjname>/cps8601_firmware.bin, where <prjname> is the tablet's ro.boot.prjname.
Project numbers seen: 23926, 23927, 23976, 23978 (Pad Pro / Pad 2), and 24926, 24976 (Pad 2 Pro family, from jjhitel's v1.0).

Every copy is 15,360 bytes. The 239xx copies share SHA-256 cfac67370d543b8b31a914a240dca5b043743388da539465260e6df6400f9e81. The 24926 copy in cxzlw's module has 33a4ab21db5e92af7f144fecf3d86f64137079d22e4890902d6da24dd6aa1ee4. No 24976 copy has been examined.
Looks like 8051 code: long jumps at the reset, INT0 and Timer0 vector slots (0x0000, 0x0003, 0x000B), and Keil C51 %bu format strings.
The strings show a Qi-style transmitter: cmd enter tx mode, Ping:Freq=…, ploss fod trigger, q cali, save Q value, RX remove, low power, start crc check, equipment (factory) mode, ver%bu.%bu.
No strings about vibration, haptics or Bluetooth.
Hashes for every examined file: research/reference/oplus-global-pen-enabler/MANIFEST.md. The binaries are not stored in this repository.
records.basis: Files from the cxzlw repo, hashed and string-scanned on 2 Nov 2026.

records.title: HID Haptics usage page (0x0E)
records.summary: The standard HID vocabulary for haptic waveforms and controls, with the IDs Windows pens use.
details: Controls: Simple Haptic Controller 0x01, Waveform List 0x10, Duration List 0x11, Auto Trigger 0x20, Manual Trigger 0x21, Auto Trigger Associated Control 0x22, Intensity 0x23, Repeat Count 0x24, Retrigger Period 0x25, Waveform Cutoff Time 0x28.
Discrete waveforms: None 0x1001, Stop 0x1002, Click 0x1003, Press 0x1006, Release 0x1007, Hover 0x1008, Success 0x1009, Error 0x100A, Collide 0x1012, Align 0x1013, Step 0x1014, Grow 0x1015.

Continuous waveforms: BuzzContinuous 0x1004, RumbleContinuous 0x1005, InkContinuous 0x100B, PencilContinuous 0x100C, MarkerContinuous 0x100D, ChiselMarkerContinuous 0x100E, BrushContinuous 0x100F, EraserContinuous 0x1010, SparkleContinuous 0x1011.
Required for Windows haptic pens: None, Stop, Click and InkContinuous. Press and Release come as a pair, as do Success and Error.
0x1012 to 0x1015 were added by the HUTRR118 expansion.
The app API calls 0x1011 GalaxyPenContinuous; the hardware guide calls it SparkleContinuous. Both describe a multi-coloured special brush.
records.basis: Microsoft haptic pen and input haptics guides, read on 2 Nov 2026.

records.title: OnePlus developer SDK for approved apps
records.summary: The official route for third-party apps: a OnePlus SDK that authenticates each app with OnePlus.
details: Verified in the README: approved third-party apps such as HiPaint go through it, and the stock Notes app uses a different, bundled SDK.
Unknown: whether it is publicly available, how an app applies, and what it requires.
records.basis: Repository README.

records.title: Haptic session call sequence (as implemented)
records.summary: The order of calls the repository's client makes to turn Stylo 2 writing feedback on and off.
details: 1. checkSelfPermission(com.oplus.permission.safe.IOT). Stop with PermissionDenied if it is not granted.
2. bindService(ACTION_PENCIL_SDK, package com.oplus.ipemanager). If it returns false the service is unavailable.
3. onServiceConnected: compare binder.interfaceDescriptor with com.oplus.ipemanager.sdk.ISdkAidlInterface before calling anything.
4. setVibrationType(preset ordinal).
5. startFeedBackVibration(). The README describes this as turning on writing feedback system-wide; the service handles the pen.
6. stopFeedBackVibration() to turn it off.
7. unbindService(). The current code does this before step 6, which should be swapped.
Connection states exposed to the UI: DISCONNECTED, CONNECTING, CONNECTED_SDK, CONNECTED_WRONG_IFACE, ERROR.
records.basis: OplusPencilSdkClient.kt and MainActivity.kt

records.title: ISDKAidlCallback: service-to-app events
records.summary: Callback interface an app registers to hear about pen connection and switch changes.
details: Descriptor: com.oplus.ipemanager.sdk.ISDKAidlCallback
1 onConnectionChanged(int state)
2 onVibrationSwitchStateChange(boolean)
3 onFunctionFeedbackStateChange(boolean)
4 onDemoModeEnableChange(boolean)
All four are one-way (FLAG_ONEWAY), so the service never waits on the app.
Registered with transaction 9 and removed with transaction 10. The current app does not register one yet.
records.basis: app/src/main/java/com/oplus/ipemanager/sdk/ISDKAidlCallback.java

records.title: IpeFeature
records.summary: Parcelable enum of service features, written to a Parcel as its ordinal.
details: DEMO_MODE = 0
FUNCTION_VIBRATION = 1
FEEDBACK_VIBRATION = 2
It is not used by any call in the current interface. It is likely related to the feature list.
records.basis: app/src/main/java/com/oplus/ipemanager/sdk/IpeFeature.java

records.title: com.oplus.ipemanager pen service and binding
records.summary: The OnePlus system service that owns the Stylo 2 link. Apps bind to it, and it does the Bluetooth work.
details: Package: com.oplus.ipemanager
Service: com.oplus.ipemanager/.btadsorb.CoreService
Bind with Intent("com.oplus.ipemanager.ACTION.PENCIL_SDK").setPackage("com.oplus.ipemanager") and BIND_AUTO_CREATE.
Required permission: com.oplus.permission.safe.IOT. The README calls it a restricted system permission that ordinary apps cannot be granted.
On Android 11 and later the client manifest needs <queries> entries for the package and the action to see the service.
Callers never send Bluetooth packets. The service talks to the pen.
Who gets access (from the README): the stock Notes app holds the permission and binds through a bundled SDK; approved third-party apps use a separate OnePlus developer SDK; any other app is refused.
records.basis: AndroidManifest.xml, OplusPencilSdkClient.kt and README in this repository.

records.title: PencilManagerUnitClient (reported client class)
records.summary: Client-side class name reported by the community as part of OnePlus's pen SDK in apps such as StarNote.
details: Named in ReVanced issue #180 as the possible place where the calling app's signature is checked.
Not present in this repository and not checked against any installed package.
records.basis: Research inventory.

records.title: ISdkAidlInterface: transaction table
records.summary: The Binder interface the pen service returns. Twelve numbered calls cover state queries, vibration control and callback registration.
details: Descriptor: com.oplus.ipemanager.sdk.ISdkAidlInterface
1 getPencilConnectState() returns int
2 getVibrationSwitchState() returns boolean
3 isFunctionVibrationEnable() returns boolean
4 isDemoModeEnable() returns boolean
5 enableDemoMode(boolean)
6 getSuportSdkVersion() returns int (spelled this way in the source)
7 setVibrationType(int)
8 startVibration(int)
9 setISdkAidlCallback(ISDKAidlCallback)
10 unsetISdkAidlCallback(ISDKAidlCallback)
11 startFeedBackVibration()
12 stopFeedBackVibration()
All calls are two-way (flags 0) and read an exception header from the reply. Booleans travel as int 0 or 1.
getSupportFeatureList() returning List<String> is declared in the Java interface but has no transaction code.
records.basis: app/src/main/java/com/oplus/ipemanager/sdk/ISdkAidlInterface.java

records.title: Vibration presets (setVibrationType values)
records.summary: The tool textures the Stylo 2 can play, sent as enum ordinals.
details: PENCIL = 0
ERASER = 1
BALLPEN = 2
PEN = 3
FUNCTION_VIBRATION = 4
The client sends type.ordinal to setVibrationType(int).
The README says these profiles come from the stock Notes app.
Whether 4 is meaningful for setVibrationType, or belongs to startVibration(int), is not documented.

records.title: oplus_wireless_pen kernel driver
records.summary: Kernel module for the pen's magnetic wireless charger (CPS8601). It detects attach and passes the pen's Bluetooth address on for pairing.
details: File: /vendor/lib/modules/oplus_wireless_pen.ko
Descriptions: "Wireless Pen Charger Cps8601" and "QTI Glink wireless pen driver". Licence GPL v2.
alias i2c:cps-wls-charger, so the chip sits on an I2C bus.
Depends on panel_event_notifier, oplus_bsp_boot_projectinfo and pmic_glink. The project-info dependency suggests it selects firmware by hardware variant.
vermagic 6.1.68-android14-11-o-g2ba5638f614f (Pad Pro / Pad 2). The Pad 3 may differ.
Log prefix [cps8601]. Key lines: Rx attach!, tx wakeup!, receive ask pkt!, [cps_wls_get_ask_packet]get ble addr, cps8601_valid_check, report 1.
Because it is GPL v2, its source should appear in OnePlus's kernel releases.
records.basis: modinfo output and kernel log quoted in the cxzlw README.

records.title: Windows haptic pen device contract
records.summary: How a pen exposes its motor to the host over plain HID, and how continuous textures start and stop.
details: Transport: HID over Bluetooth with Windows inbox drivers.
Top-level collection: Digitizers page 0x0D, Stylus usage 0x20, containing a Simple Haptic Controller collection (page 0x0E, usage 0x01).

Identity: the digitizer and the Bluetooth stylus collection must both report Transducer Serial Number (0x0D/0x5B, 32-bit, optional Part 2 at 0x6E) and Transducer Vendor ID (0x0D/0x91). This lets the OS tell which pen made which stroke. It is mandatory for haptics.
Discovery: a GET_FEATURE report lists the supported waveforms and their durations (Waveform List 0x10, Duration List 0x11). Continuous waveforms have duration 0.
Command: an OUTPUT report sets Manual Trigger (0x21) to an ordinal, plus optional Intensity 0 to 100 (0x23), Repeat Count (0x24), Retrigger Period (0x25) and Waveform Cutoff Time (0x28).
Ordinal 1 is None and 2 is Stop. Ordinals from 3 index the device's waveform list.

A discrete waveform plays immediately. A continuous waveform is configured and then played at the pen's discretion, for example when it detects tip contact. Microsoft notes this departs from the HID spec because Windows does not use Auto Trigger.
States: Playing, Paused (configured, not touching), Stopped. Clearing the configuration when the pen leaves range is recommended.
The pen digitizer protocol is left open. A protocol with an uplink from screen to pen can be used to modulate the haptics.
Optional tail button over Bluetooth LE keyboard reports: WIN+F20 click, WIN+F19 double-click, WIN+F18 press and hold.
records.basis: Microsoft Haptic Pen Implementation Guide, read on 2 Nov 2026.

records.title: Windows pen haptics API (PenDevice + SimpleHapticsController)
records.summary: App-side model: get the pen from a pointer event, pick a named waveform it supports, send it, and stop when the pointer leaves.
details: Classes: PenDevice, SimpleHapticsController, KnownSimpleHapticsControllerWaveforms. In the Windows App SDK, PenDeviceInterop.FromPointerPoint().

Inking waveforms play continuously while the pen touches the screen: InkContinuous (required, fallback), BrushContinuous, PencilContinuous, MarkerContinuous, ChiselMarkerContinuous, EraserContinuous, GalaxyPenContinuous.
Interaction waveforms: Click (required, fallback), Error, Hover, Press, Release, Success, BuzzContinuous, RumbleContinuous.
Pick from SupportedFeedback, then SendHapticFeedback(waveform) or SendHapticFeedback(waveform, intensity).
Call StopFeedback() on PointerExited. Some pens stop on lift by themselves, but not all.
Optional settings, each with a support check: intensity, play count, play duration, replay pause interval.
Windows 11 only. Check that the SimpleHapticsController property exists before using it.
records.basis: Microsoft Learn page, read on 2 Nov 2026.

records.title: Xiaomi Pencil Engine (PenEngine AAR)
records.summary: Xiaomi's app-facing stylus SDK. It covers input features and gestures, but the published API list has no explicit haptic motor command.
details: Packages: com.miui.penengine.ocr, .estimate, .onestroke, .hover, .posture, .colorpick, .touchfilm, .auth
Capabilities: stroke prediction, one-stroke shape recognition, handwriting recognition, cross-app colour picking, pen rotation and posture, hover preview, Focus Pen Pro touch-button gestures.
Includes authentication classes. Apps must be registered with Xiaomi.
Most useful as an example of how to structure a vendor-neutral, app-facing API.
records.basis: Research inventory, from dev.mi.com.
